IR.rationale: REITs are long-duration, bond-like equities, so a rise in intermediate yields relative to the policy rate raises discount rates and financing costs and pressures REIT valuations over the following weeks.

B.rationale: Leveraged real estate depends on credit availability. Stable or narrowing Baa spreads combined with strong high-yield returns describe easy credit conditions that support REIT prices.

V.rationale: High equity implied volatility signals elevated risk premia, which theory and evidence link to higher subsequent expected returns once the shock has been priced.

AP.rationale: REITs carry substantial equity beta and adjust to broad market moves with a lag, so recent market excess returns carry short-horizon information for REITs.

ST.rationale: The short-term reversal factor captures liquidity-provision returns. When it is strong, recent losers such as rate-hit REITs tend to rebound.

FX.rationale: A strengthening broad dollar tightens global financial conditions and often accompanies rising real rates, which weighs on income-oriented, rate-sensitive assets.

COM.rationale: Broad commodity gains signal reflation and stronger nominal growth, which feed through to rents and real-asset demand but can also raise inflation-driven rate risk.

MC.rationale: Tight aggregate financial conditions restrict real-estate financing and coincide with high risk premia, both of which are informative for subsequent REIT returns.

ENDG.rationale: Index returns over weekly to quarterly horizons show short-term reversal and intermediate momentum, so the index's own recent performance is informative.

IR.rationale: Sharp moves up in intermediate yields are rate shocks that REITs are especially exposed to, and they raise subsequent REIT variance.

B.rationale: Widening spreads together with falling high-yield prices mark credit stress, which raises future equity and real-estate volatility through leverage and funding channels.

V.rationale: Implied volatility forecasts realised volatility beyond its own history. Combined with high policy uncertainty it identifies broad uncertainty regimes that persist.

AP.rationale: Through the leverage and volatility-feedback effects, negative market returns predict higher future volatility.

ST.rationale: Momentum drawdowns tend to occur in turbulent, rebounding markets, so weak momentum returns flag unstable regimes with elevated volatility.

FX.rationale: Yen appreciation is a classic safe-haven, risk-off signal associated with carry unwinds and higher subsequent risk-asset volatility.

COM.rationale: Oil price slumps can signal growth fears and stress for leveraged energy credits, which spills over into broader volatility.

MC.rationale: Financial stress indices aggregate funding, credit and volatility strains and predict elevated realised volatility ahead.

ENDG.rationale: Volatility clusters, and very high recent variance tends to decay toward its mean, so its own level informs the residual forecast.

IR.rationale: Abrupt rises in intermediate yields, as in taper-type shocks, are the main source of sharp REIT drawdowns.

B.rationale: Deteriorating credit conditions raise the risk of a forced deleveraging sell-off in leveraged real estate.

V.rationale: High implied volatility widens the return distribution and raises the probability of left-tail outcomes.

AP.rationale: Weak market returns signal risk-off dynamics and declining risk appetite that can extend into REIT losses.

ST.rationale: Momentum crashes and factor unwinds coincide with disorderly markets in which tail losses are more likely.

FX.rationale: A sharp dollar rally signals tightening global dollar funding conditions, which raises the risk of losses in rate- and liquidity-sensitive assets.

COM.rationale: Falling commodity prices point to weakening global demand and deflationary risk-off episodes.

MC.rationale: Elevated financial stress raises the probability of disorderly selling and large drawdowns.

ENDG.rationale: Recent losses coincide with high-volatility states, in which further left-tail outcomes are more likely.

IR.rationale: Falling intermediate yields lower discount rates and favour bond proxies, so they set up strong REIT rallies.

B.rationale: Strong high-yield returns signal improving risk appetite and credit availability, which supports large REIT gains.

V.rationale: High volatility widens both tails, and high risk premia make sharp rebounds more likely.

AP.rationale: Strong broad equity markets carry over to REITs through their equity beta.

ST.rationale: Strong reversal returns indicate rebounds in recently sold assets, consistent with right-tail recoveries.

FX.rationale: A weakening dollar eases global financial conditions and supports risk assets and yield-seeking flows.

COM.rationale: Rising commodity prices signal reflation and growth, which favour real assets.

MC.rationale: Large gains tend to follow periods of tight conditions, when depressed prices and high risk premia allow sharp relief rallies.

ENDG.rationale: After weak recent returns, reversal and high volatility raise the chance of a large rebound.
